title: 3D Interactive vs Aurora UI
lede: Both are dark, both are blue, both move. The difference is whether the depth is in the objects or in the air behind them.
verdict: 3D interactive puts depth on the elements: stacked text-shadow on the headline, cards that lift 3px on hover and tilt toward the pointer. Aurora puts depth in the background: three blurred radial fields drifting on 14 to 22 second cycles behind panels that barely move.
brief: The 3D page earns its name from two things — a headline built from a multi-line text-shadow stack that imitates extrusion, and cards at 10px radius with a 1px #7f9bff border and a 0 10px 24px -10px blue shadow. Interaction is the point: hover translates the card up 3px, and the tilt follows the pointer.

Aurora is a background technique. Three circles at 50% radius, each a radial gradient fading to transparent at 66%, animated with small translate and scale keyframes so they drift out of sync. The panels in front use backdrop-filter: blur(14px) and a 1px rgba(255,255,255,.18) border — they are glass, and they are deliberately static.

dimensions.name: Where depth lives
dimensions.a: On the elements — shadow stack and lift
dimensions.b: In the background — drifting colour fields

dimensions.name: Cost
dimensions.a: Transform per card; cheap but needs throttling
dimensions.b: Three composited layers; needs a pause control

dimensions.name: Touch behaviour
dimensions.a: Must be disabled — no hover on a phone
dimensions.b: Works as-is; nothing depends on a pointer

cssDelta.label: Headline
cssDelta.b: no shadow; a dark scrim behind the text

whenA: The page is a product or a demo where the interaction itself is the argument
There are few cards and the user will actually point at them
You can gate the effect behind a hover media query so phones get the flat state
whenB: The page is a hero or a landing section where atmosphere matters more than interaction
You want the site to feel alive with no input at all — a kiosk, a launch page, a title screen
You need the effect to work identically on touch
promptDelta: Split the instruction between object and air. For 3D, say the depth is a multi-layer text-shadow with 1px steps and that cards tilt on hover toward the pointer, with perspective on the parent. For aurora, say the depth is three radial gradients at 50% radius drifting on different durations behind static glass panels. A model asked for "dark 3D glassmorphism" will do both at once — moving fields under cards that also have drop shadows and tilt — and three depth cues will fight each other.
